## Proof

**Setup.** The local ring $\mathbb{Z}_{\langle 5\rangle}$ is the localization of $\mathbb{Z}$ at the prime ideal $(5)$:
$$\mathbb{Z}_{\langle 5\rangle} = \left\{\frac{a}{b}\in\mathbb{Q} : a,b\in\mathbb{Z},\; 5\nmid b\right\}.$$
Its unique maximal ideal is
$$5\mathbb{Z}_{\langle 5\rangle} = \left\{\frac{a}{b}\in\mathbb{Z}_{\langle 5\rangle} : 5\mid a\right\}.$$
The residue field is the quotient $\mathbb{Z}_{\langle 5\rangle}\,/\,5\mathbb{Z}_{\langle 5\rangle}$.

**General fact.** For any commutative ring $R$ and prime ideal $\mathfrak{p}\subset R$, the residue field of the local ring $R_{\mathfrak{p}}$ is naturally isomorphic to the fraction field of $R/\mathfrak{p}$:
$$R_{\mathfrak{p}}/\mathfrak{p}R_{\mathfrak{p}} \;\cong\; \operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak{p}).$$

*Proof of the fact.* Define
$$\varphi: R_{\mathfrak{p}} \to \operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak{p}),\qquad \varphi\!\left(\frac{a}{s}\right) = \frac{\overline{a}}{\overline{s}},$$
where $\overline{a},\overline{s}$ denote images in $R/\mathfrak{p}$. This is well defined: since $s\notin\mathfrak{p}$, the class $\overline{s}$ is nonzero in the integral domain $R/\mathfrak{p}$, hence a unit in its fraction field. It is a ring homomorphism, and its kernel is
$$\ker\varphi = \left\{\frac{a}{s}\in R_{\mathfrak{p}} : \overline{a}=0\right\} = \left\{\frac{a}{s}: a\in\mathfrak{p}\right\} = \mathfrak{p}R_{\mathfrak{p}}.$$
It is surjective: any element $\frac{\overline{a}}{\overline{s}}\in\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak{p})$ with $\overline{s}\neq 0$ (i.e. $s\notin\mathfrak{p}$) is the image of $\frac{a}{s}\in R_{\mathfrak{p}}$. By the first isomorphism theorem,
$$R_{\mathfrak{p}}/\mathfrak{p}R_{\mathfrak{p}} \cong \operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak{p}). \qquad\blacksquare$$

**Application.** Take $R=\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathfrak{p}=(5)$. Then
$$R/\mathfrak{p} = \mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z} = \mathbb{F}_5,$$
which is already a field (since $5$ is prime), so
$$\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak{p}) = \operatorname{Frac}(\mathbb{F}_5) = \mathbb{F}_5.$$

**Direct verification (optional).** The map
$$\mathbb{Z}_{\langle 5\rangle} \to \mathbb{F}_5,\qquad \frac{a}{b}\mapsto a\,b^{-1}\pmod{5}$$
is well defined (since $5\nmid b$, $b$ is invertible mod $5$), surjective (every class $\bar n\in\mathbb{F}_5$ is the image of $\frac{n}{1}$), and has kernel exactly $5\mathbb{Z}_{\langle 5\rangle}$. Hence
$$\mathbb{Z}_{\langle 5\rangle}\,/\,5\mathbb{Z}_{\langle 5\rangle} \;\cong\; \mathbb{F}_5.$$

**Conclusion.** The residue field of $\mathbb{Z}_{\langle 5\rangle}$ with respect to its maximal ideal $5\mathbb{Z}_{\langle 5\rangle}$ is

$$\boxed{\,\mathbb{Z}_{\langle 5\rangle}\,/\,5\mathbb{Z}_{\langle 5\rangle}\;\cong\;\mathbb{F}_5\,=\;\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}\,}.$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
